title: Terminal commands act on data, not scenes: a Subsystem tag per command, the knot/model/ring data off the scene, one Scene.dataset lookup
description:
Terminal commands know scenes instead of the data they act on. 18 of the 29 commands open with `if (!(terminal.scene instanceof MainScene editor))` (or ModelScene / RingScene), build their own refusal, and then read fields off the scene: the scene is used as the data store. User direction (2026-10-18): the scene is the display; the interaction and the data are separate. Each command tags the subsystem it acts on, and the scene only says which data it shows.

What each command acts on (ENG-31 worktree):
- TERMINAL (history, working directory): cl, cd, chk
- TOGGLES (global Toggle): tgl
- listing: ls (files, commands, tools, toggles, keys)
- FILES (.ix files on disk via FileManagement): ld, nw, rld, sv, ut, add, cmt (add and cmt take the file from MainScene.tempFile / file today)
- KNOT (the multi-level knot structure and the point set it is built from: resultKnots, subPaths, tourShell, orgShell, totalLayers, tourLength): ck, ask, mv, mb, ma, sg, updt. A tour is one cycle read off the knot; the subsystem is KNOT.
- VIEW (camera, active tool, colours, leaving the view): ct, rst, clr, ex
- MODEL (DSL model, graph overrides, model collection): ml, set, cn
- RINGS (ring waypoints, working DSL, regions): rg, xp

Design (no new data classes, no renames):
1. A Subsystem enum (TERMINAL, TOGGLES, FILES, KNOT, VIEW, MODEL, RINGS); @CommandAnnotation gains `acts = Subsystem.X`.
2. Each subsystem's data is an existing object the scene holds, not scene fields:
   - KNOT: PointSetPath (it already holds ps, tsp, d, comments, grid); MainScene's resultKnots, subPaths, tourShell, orgShell, totalLayers, tourLength and file/tempFile move onto it. MainScene holds one PointSetPath and draws it; the knot tools read it there. Note the name clash: Knot is the single-knot class in geometry/tsp/knot, so the dataset is PointSetPath, not a new Knot-named class.
   - MODEL: NodeGraphRuntime (already owns the run and its overrides; ModelScene.overrides, a second copy, goes) plus ModelCollection.
   - RINGS: SurfaceRing plus RegionLayer.
   - VIEW: the scene itself, the one subsystem that is the display.
   - TERMINAL, TOGGLES, FILES: Terminal, Toggle, FileManagement, already scene-free.
3. One lookup is the only scene-command link: Scene.dataset(Subsystem) returns what the scene shows for that subsystem, or null. The terminal resolves it before running a command, refuses in one place ("mv acts on a knot; this scene shows none"), and hands the command the typed object (PointSetPath, not MainScene). ls commands lists only commands whose subsystem the scene provides.
4. Commands spanning two subsystems: clr is VIEW and also asks for KNOT (it reads the knots to colour them); xp is RINGS and sets the explode amount on RegionLayer instead of switching to the region tool.
No command keeps an instanceof on a scene type.
definition-of-done:
1. Every @CommandAnnotation names the Subsystem it acts on; no terminal command has an instanceof on a scene type.
2. MainScene's knot data lives on its PointSetPath; ModelScene.overrides is gone (NodeGraphRuntime owns overrides).
3. Scene.dataset(Subsystem) is the only place a scene says what commands can act on; the terminal refuses unsupported commands in one place and ls commands lists only supported ones.
4. Every command behaves as before in ixdar-canvas, mesh-viewer and ring-tool, including the refusals.
5. Full test suite and test_cli pass.

6. The terminal ring command rg/ring (RingCommand) is deleted (user, 2026-10-21; CRAW-74 made `ixdar-cli rings add --points` the one path from surface points to a confirmed, saved ring), together with the RingScene state only it used: ringWaypointsXyz, ringWaypointCount, ring, closeRing, clearRing, showRing, RING_SEED_LABEL, RING_TIGHTENED_LABEL. This settles where the rg waypoints live: nowhere. Its before-transcript lines become "unknown command".
7. The MODEL subsystem's data is the scene's ModelCollection, which holds the requested model and the overrides since VIEW-27; read "NodeGraphRuntime owns overrides" in the description and item 2 as ModelCollection, and ModelScene.overrides is already gone.

8. User rulings 2026-10-21 on the agent's design gate:
   - ask: Segment/Knot hyperstrings take the zoom and hover actions as callbacks the scene supplies, so ask acts on KNOT data alone and keeps its clickable, hoverable links.
   - rst and ex work in every scene through Scene methods: rst camera frames everything, rst tool deactivates and reactivates the active tool, ex is the scene's Esc; the mesh-viewer and ring-tool refusals go.
   - xp: the explosion moves onto RegionLayer, shows under every tool and no longer collapses when the region tool is switched off.
   - @CommandAnnotation has one array attribute `acts` (a single value needs no braces, e.g. `acts = Subsystem.KNOT`, `acts = {Subsystem.VIEW, Subsystem.KNOT}`); the terminal refuses when the scene lacks any listed subsystem, and the command asks for each dataset by subsystem.
   - A scene's datasets do not outlive the scene (the ticket's default).
testing-plan:
1. Before/after transcript of every command in ixdar-canvas, mesh-viewer and ring-tool through ixdar-cli terminal --line (including ones that must refuse); diff.
2. Screenshots of the tour editor after mv, clr and rst, and the ring scene after xp.
changes-made: Subsystem enum (annotations module) and a required @CommandAnnotation acts array on every command; the command registry processor emits CommandRegistry_Commands.ACTS. Scene.dataset(Subsystem) is the one scene-command link (VIEW = the scene; MainScene adds KNOT = its PointSetPath, ModelScene MODEL = its ModelCollection, RingScene RINGS = its RegionLayer). Terminal.refusal is the one refusal ('mv acts on a knot; this scene shows none'), used by run, runNoArgs and ls commands; commands read data via Terminal.dataset. No command has a scene instanceof (18 before).

Knot data moved onto PointSetPath: file, tempFile, tourShell, resultKnots, subPaths, totalLayers, tourLength, plus the knot colours clr rewrites (stickyColor, metroColors, knotGradientColors); orgShell is PointSetPath.tsp. MainScene holds one pointSetPath (was retTup) and supplies hover/focus callbacks on it, which Segment/Knot/CutMatchList hyperstrings now take, so ask keeps clickable links on KNOT data alone. Scene.escapePressed is the Esc every scene shares (MainScene.back became its override; MenuScene steps out of a submenu); ex and rst work through Scene methods in every scene.

MODEL: ml/set/cn act on ModelCollection; ModelScene hands it three callbacks (offered models, requestLoad, validateOverrideKey) that open() carries, the same scene-supplied-callback shape as the ask ruling; ModelScene.requestModel removed. RINGS: RingCommand (rg) deleted with RingScene.addRingWaypoint and clearRing; the explosion moved from RingRegionTool onto RegionLayer, stepped and shown in every tool, no collapse on leaving the region tool; xp sets it without switching tools. ringWaypointsXyz/ringWaypointCount/ring/closeRing/showRing/RING_*_LABEL stay: the rings add route (Add.java) and ui-state still use them on master; CRAW-74 (REVIEW) rewrites Add.

Verification: before/after terminal transcripts of 58/62/62 lines in ixdar-canvas/mesh-viewer/ring-tool (tmp/eng-37-before, tmp/eng-37-after, tmp/eng-37-diff.py): knot editor outputs unchanged except refusal wording, ls commands filtering and rg now unknown; mesh-viewer/ring-tool refusals now come from the terminal, rst/ex now run there, ck (a no-op) is refused outside the knot editor. Screenshots tmp/eng-37-editor-after-{mv,clr,rst}.png, tmp/eng-37-ring-{before,after}-xp.png (fertility_rings, 10 regions exploded in the orbit tool). Tests: MainSceneTerminalCommandTest +4 (one-place refusal, rst/ex in a knot-less scene, ls commands filtering, ask links drive the editor's hover through the callbacks); mvn test 572/0, test_cli 104/0.
review-summary: Terminal commands now name the subsystem they act on and get its data from one scene lookup: the knot editor's knot lives on PointSetPath, models on ModelCollection, ring regions on RegionLayer. Commands no longer test scene types, so the terminal refuses in one place and lists only runnable commands.
